questions.explanation: Each of the twelve major keys has one relative minor, giving twelve relative pairs.
questions.hint: One relative minor per major key.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Why the circle of fifths is ordered as it is
questions.learningObjective: Identify enharmonic equivalents on the circle
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note asks which keys are enharmonic on the circle of fifths; which pair is correct?

options.text: F major and D minor, relative keys
C major and G major, adjacent keys
D major and B minor, relative keys
Gb major and F# major, same pitches different names

questions.explanation: Gb major and F# major are enharmonic: same pitches, different names. They sit at the same point on the circle.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: The leading tone and its pull
questions.learningObjective: Identify the leading tone in F major
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note in F major asks for the leading tone; which note is it?

options.text: Eb, a whole step below the tonic
options.misconception: forgets E natural in F major

options.text: E, a half step below the tonic F

questions.explanation: In F major, the seventh degree is E, a half step below F. That is the leading tone.
questions.hint: Seventh degree of F major is E.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Subdominant and dominant function
questions.learningObjective: Explain functional harmony basics
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note asks what functional harmony describes; explain briefly.

answer.exemplar: Functional harmony describes how chords relate to the tonic, with tonic as home, subdominant as departure, and dominant as tension seeking resolution.

questions.explanation: Functional harmony assigns roles: tonic is home, subdominant departs, dominant creates tension that resolves to tonic.
questions.hint: Tonic home, subdominant departure, dominant tension.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Chords built in thirds and the numeral that names them
questions.learningObjective: Count thirds in a seventh chord
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note asks how many thirds stack to form a seventh chord; state the count.
questions.explanation: A seventh chord stacks three thirds: root to third, third to fifth, fifth to seventh.
questions.hint: Three thirds make a seventh chord.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What an inversion does to quality and number
questions.learningObjective: Invert a perfect fourth
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note inverts a perfect fourth; what interval results?
questions.explanation: A perfect fourth is five semitones. Its inversion is twelve minus five, seven semitones, a perfect fifth.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: What a key signature holds
questions.learningObjective: Identify the tonic of a key signature
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note shows no sharps or flats; which major key is indicated?
questions.explanation: No sharps or flats indicates C major (or A minor). The major key is C major.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Relative major and relative minor
questions.learningObjective: Explain the distance between relative tonics
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note asks why relative keys are a minor third apart; explain briefly.

answer.exemplar: Relative keys are a minor third apart because the minor tonic sits three semitones below the major tonic, sharing the same scale degrees.

questions.explanation: The relative minor tonic is three semitones below the major tonic. That interval is a minor third.
questions.hint: Three semitones is a minor third.

questions.subject: MUSIC_THEORY
questions.topic: Why the circle of fifths is ordered as it is
questions.learningObjective: Explain the circle's practical use
questions.stem: An analyst's dashboard note asks how many flats the key at the far left of the circle has; state the count.
questions.explanation: The far left of the circle (counterclockwise) reaches six flats, Gb major (or F# major enharmonically). Six flats is the maximum common key.
questions.hint: Six flats at the far left.
